Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 01-Jan-2026 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE,  
  MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - JANUARY 2026  
  Deep Learning [IT_4442]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                 Evaluate the causes of overfitting and discuss the methods used to mitigate it in machine learning   (5)  
  models.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)            Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of unsupervised learning algorithms in real-world              (5)  
  applications such as customer segmentation or anomaly detection.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
2)                 Evaluate the role of activation functions in deep feedforward networks. How does the choice of       (5)  
  activation function affect the performance of the model?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)            Evaluate the effect of different learning rates during the backpropagation process. How does an      (5)  
  inappropriate learning rate impact model convergence?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
3)                 Analyze the impact of data augmentation on the training time and model accuracy. Does                (5)  
  augmentation always lead to better performance in deep learning models?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)            Analyze the difference between early stopping and regularization in terms of their effect on model   (5)  
  performance. In which situations would one be preferred over the other?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)                 Compare the effectiveness of gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent (SGD), and mini-batch     (5)  
  gradient descent. How does each method affect convergence speed and stability?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)            Analyze the architecture of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). How do convolutional layers        (5)  
  and pooling layers contribute to the feature extraction process?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

5)                       Compare the application of RNNs to other types of neural networks for tasks involving sequential    (5)  
  data, such as time-series prediction or speech recognition.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)               Analyze the benefits of using LSTMs over traditional RNNs in applications such as natural language (5)  
  processing or speech recognition. How does LSTM address the vanishing gradient problem?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  -----End-----
